profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the applied ML research lead and the ML platform engineer for an internal fraud-risk modeling project that is moving from notebook-driven experimentation to an automated retraining-and-deployment workflow. The immediate context is that the research team has a candidate gradient-boosted model and wants it folded into the organization’s CI/CD-style MLOps stack before an upcoming architecture review. The agenda is to align on the handoff artifact from research to platform, confirm what environment the first deployment target will be, check whether the model is 'ready for automation,' and clarify what monitoring needs to be wired in after deployment. The expected outcome is a shared plan for next week’s handoff and a rough division of responsibilities between the research and platform workstreams.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Gradient-boosted models, experiment design, reproducibility, offline evaluation
members.background: Lena leads a small research group that prototypes risk models for internal products; she came from an academic ML lab and has gradually adopted MLflow, DVC, and containerized training for internal handoffs.
members.private_state: She wants the platform team to absorb operational complexity quickly so her group can move on to feature work, and she is trying to present the current model as mature enough for automation without inviting a long rework cycle.
hidden_assumptions: A 'training bundle' is primarily a research reproducibility package: code revision, config file, metrics summary, and a reference model artifact.
When teams say they will 'push to staging,' they usually mean the offline validation namespace where batch scoring can run safely against holdout data.
A model is 'ready for automation' once repeated training runs are stable, logged, and reproducible, even if execution still assumes a human-triggered workflow.
Monitoring for a first deployment mainly means model-quality telemetry like score distributions and drift, while service-level instrumentation is standard platform plumbing.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: Kubeflow pipelines, CI/CD integration, artifact registries, deployment orchestration, model observability
members.background: Ravi maintains the company’s shared MLOps platform and is responsible for standardizing model packaging and deployment contracts across several applied ML teams.
members.private_state: He wants this project to conform to the platform template with minimal custom support, and he is concerned about taking on hidden operational obligations that the research team may assume are already covered.
hidden_assumptions: A 'training bundle' is a deployable handoff package centered on the pipeline spec, container digest, environment lock, schema contract, and data snapshot identifier rather than a single trained model file.
When teams say 'staging,' they mean the pre-production serving cluster that mirrors production APIs and infra behavior.
A model is only 'ready for automation' when it can run unattended on schedule with pinned environments, secret handling, retries, and contract-compliant outputs.
Monitoring includes end-to-end operational hooks by default, but model-specific quality joins require the research team to provide label mapping and business-level feature semantics.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Lena will hand over the 'training bundle' next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the bundle is the research handoff: git commit/tag, training config YAML, MLflow run link, metrics report, and a reference model artifact.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the bundle is the platform handoff: pipeline definition, container image digest, environment lockfile, schema contract, and data snapshot/version references needed to rebuild and deploy.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams already use the phrase internally and it sounds like a routine artifact name; because each assumes the other is using the team's obvious default, neither thinks to enumerate contents.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the model should go to 'staging' before anything broader.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the offline ml-staging namespace used for nightly batch scoring on the frozen June holdout and qualitative inspection of outputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the pre-production serving cluster called staging that exposes the same API contract as production and receives mirrored low-volume traffic.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Pushing to staging is a standard step and both environments are commonly called 'staging' across teams; the phrase signals prudent rollout rather than a point needing clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align that the current pipeline is almost 'ready for automation.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means the training job reproduces within expected variance across repeated runs, logs lineage in MLflow/DVC, and can be kicked off from a clean container by a person.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means the whole retraining pipeline can run unattended under CI/CD or a scheduler, with secret injection, failure retries, pinned environments, validation gates, and deployable outputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely discussing maturity rather than disputing direction, and 'ready for automation' functions like a progress label whose exact threshold usually remains implicit.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to add the monitoring hooks in the first pass.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes prediction distributions, feature drift summaries, and delayed quality dashboards once batch labels arrive; latency and serving health are generic platform concerns outside her workstream.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes service metrics, request/response logging, schema checks, and only the basic interfaces needed for later quality joins; label joins and business-quality definitions are still part of the research team's deliverable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a low-level implementation detail already covered by standard practice, so each person mentally includes their obvious subset and hears no contradiction in the other's agreement.

I need to keep this moving toward the architecture review without opening a giant redesign of the research workflow.
